design_note: Turn autonomy into a concrete capability policy for four specialist roles. The matrix shows that approval is limited to an already permitted action class and cannot unlock an unrelated capability.

source.title: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
source.concept: Reduce unnecessary capabilities and permissions, and require independent review for high-impact actions. Downstream authorization must enforce the chosen scope.
source.scope: The four roles, resource scope and approval matrix are fictional ShopAssist configuration, not an OWASP-prescribed role model.

lesson.anchor: Build it: a mocked decision/action loop
lesson.title: Autonomy belongs to an operation and a role
lesson.intro: All operations below concern customer C-7 and verified owned resources. This fictional host policy separates automatic eligibility, required review and prohibited capabilities for four specialist roles.

data.rule: ALLOW still needs current resource checks. REVIEW adds exact approval; DENY cannot be waived.

read: Read across a role to inspect its permitted action classes.
The refund specialist needs review for money movement but cannot reset sign-in.
The same model could serve every role without receiving the same authority.
lesson.question: Can a refund reviewer approve a sign-in reset proposed by the refund specialist?
lesson.answer: No. That role has a DENY entry for sign-in reset. Approval satisfies a review condition only within an authorized action class; it cannot grant a new capability. Route the request to the authorized security process and apply its independent checks.
lesson.takeaway: Review narrows an authorized operation; it does not expand the role.
lesson.assumption: Fictional configured policy; each role has authenticated scope. ALLOW is conditional on normal checks, and REVIEW is not execution permission.
